translation:
Koizumi and I headed to the scene of the
crime to meet up with Haruhi.
…That was fine, but…

…Then, perhaps the computer society
encountered that kind of phenomenon…

…You've heard of that kind of thing before,
right? It shows up in a lot of legends, so…

As expected of Miss Suzumiya. Quite the
expert, indeed.
It's been getting awfully lively over here.
…What are you two talking about?

We were having a chat about the other
phenomena the computer society members saw.
Not about class 1-10?

Not this time. They also told us about various
other mysteries.

Perhaps they are hiding more tales…? Such is
what Miss Suzumiya was wondering.

It's easier to deal with things if you know
what to expect before you witness them, right?
Well, that's probably true.

I sincerely hope it's nothing that'll get Haruhi
too excited.

So, Koizumi. What other unnatural phenomena
do you want to occur?

The plain old seven wonders are boring, after
all.

Quite so. Passengers disappearing suddenly,
leaving just an empty vehicle, perhaps?

…Koizumi, could you stop that? Haruhi will
surely get overexcited.

Oh, that's the story about the American ship,
right?!

If I remember right, the food was left there,
still warm and everything.

Indeed. It's a deeply interesting matter,
however, the truth is as such…

The favored theory is of a sudden incident,
causing everyone to abandon ship in a hurry.

When it was discovered, everyone's
belongings were left as is, but…

It seems the idea of the food still being warm
was a mere dramatization.
Hmmm? Really…
I'd definitely like to be on one of those ships.

Summer means the sea after all, and that
means cruising on a luxury ghost liner!

Hey, Haruhi, what the hell is wrong with your
thought process?

Actually, a monster probably came from the
sea and swept all the humans away.
That just occurred to me.

Indeed, all around the world there are stor-
ies of monsters appearing here and there.

How about the Himalayan Yeti, for a famous
example?
The gold standard cryptid!

It's said to be an unknown giant humanoid
ape right?!

However, according to later research, "yeti”
is the local word for a brown bear.

And it seems what we called its fur was, in
actuality, the fur from a brown bear.

So I suppose the explorers mistook it in the
intensity of snowstorms then.

Makes me want to tell them to look properly
before announcing something like that.
It's exactly as you say.

On a similar note, there's Bigfoot in North
America, but…

Also known as the Sasquatch, right? It seems
more like an ape than the yeti.

That's right. It certainly seems like a giant
ape-man, yet once again…

The theory is that they too, are misidentified
bears with gray fur that inhabit the area.

Ehh, that's a shame. I wonder why they
mistook them.

Legends and cryptids and such; Koizumi
drip-fed Haruhi unnatural phenomena stories.

Hold on… For a while now, Koizumi has just
been bringing up this stuff only to deny it.

…Well, whenever they open the lid and reveal
the truth, it's always something else.

Hmm. Whatever the story, the twist is always
the same.
…So that's what you're doing, Koizumi.

While the story suits Haruhi, it doesn't
stimulate her curiosity more than necessary.

By doing so, you're nailing the ideas in her
head…

Right. Just to be safe, I'll strike a nail of my
own.

To put it simply, those kind of phenomena come
from mistakes or delusions.
Indeed. It's precisely as you say.

As the old Japanese saying goes, [#P05ghosts] are
no more than withered silver grass[#P00].

If you examined the bigger picture, you'd
likely find that result is surprisingly common.
That's right. It's exactly as Koizumi says.

So, don't look at silver grass in the dark and
mistake it for a ghost.

I'm not that careless, you know. My eyes are
good.

You don't get it. I'm trying to tell you not to
jump at every little thing.

If the stories all sound dreamy, it's because
they're products of your imagination, right?

Indeed. And a lot of it was produced by our
ancestors' [#P05power] of imagination[#P00].

It's amazing what the power of imagination
can do, huh?

Even if something's actually not a big deal, it
can make it feel like something incredible.
You say all that, but what about you Kyon?
Huh? What about me?

Don't you know any interesting legends that
would make me tremble in excitement?
Uh… Don't ask me.

The two of you have strange stories so
worldwide and fanatical that I can't keep up.

How rude of me. Maybe I should've gone for
more general conversation.

Don't apologize with that wry smile. Damn it,
that churns my stomach even more.

If there aren't any, you don't need to forcibly
wring them out.

There's a huge gap between our deputy bri-
gade chief Koizumi, and a low-ranker like Kyon.
It's like an insurmountable wall.
Ah, really now?

I have no interest in happy mystery chat with
these two in the first place…

But when you go that far I can't help but feel
a bit bad.

Well, he sure knows what he's talking about.
Koizumi is a [#P05superb] deputy brigade chief[#P00].
Hahaha, I'm quite flattered.

I could taste the slight flavor of sarcasm
loaded in his words.

Drop that easy smile that doesn't look
flattered at all. It's creepy.

I suppose even I can tell a few mystery
stories.
Well if you can, get on and tell them!
Ugh, w-well…

Aaah, my mind went blank since you asked so
suddenly.

Would you look at that. It's not good enough
if you can't say them immediately!

I don't want to hear anything from you until
you've licked the dirt from Koizumi's nails!

Ugh, what a horrible way of putting it, you
[#P05oppressive] brigade chief[#P01].
It's a mistake or delusion.
Isn't that a dream come true?
Agree
Refute
